 Shri S.K.Vyas - Senior Advocate with Shri L
 Chandiramani & Shri Amit Vyas - Advocates for the applicant.
 Shri Amit Raval - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/S
 Order

This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.127/2025 registered at Police Station-Jaora City, District Ratlam(M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 406 of IPC and Section 21(1), 21(2) and 21(3) of The Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019.

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant is apprehending his arrest in the matter.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.

Learned Senior Advocate for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
submits that it is a case of commercial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35417 2 MCRC-52117-2025 civil transaction with regard to non-payment of loan advanced to the applicant.

Learned counsel referring to Sections 2(7), Section 6 and Section 41 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposits Schemes Act, 2019 (referred to as 'The Act of 2019' hereinafter) contends that according to the statement of alleged depositors, the loan advanced for the business of the applicant for M/s.
Ambika Borewell does not constitute offence punishable u/S 21(3) of the Act of 2019.

sentences.text: Mahendra Chandalia has facilitated loan to the applicant from various complainants and executed promissory notes on behalf of the applicant.
Regular interest on the loan was paid to the complainants.
Due to financial constraints, when the payment of interest was deferred , false allegation of cheating and fraud are levelled against the applicant.
There was no intention to defraud the complainants from the inception.
Relevant seizures have already been made.
Custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed in the matter.
Applicant, a reputed businessman, enjoys good character and social reputation.
Jail incarceration on false accusation would cause hardship to the applicant and his dependent family.
He is ready to cooperate in the investigation.
He intends to repay and settle the dispute.
The applicant has already deposited Rs. 50 Lakhs before the trial Court to show his bonafide.
No criminal antecedents is reported against the applicant .
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and business.
There is no likelihood tampering with evidence as the prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
Considering the advanced age of the applicant, he be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35417 3 MCRC-52117-2025 application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel contends that any kind of advance money or loan, with promise of return with or without benefit in form of interest, is covered u/S 2(4) of the Act, 2019.
Therefore, offence punishable u/S 21(3) of the Act of 2019 is prima-facie made out against the applicant.
The applicant was not available for investigation earlier.
Therefore, the bail application is meritless.

However,
after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

According to the material available on case diary, Hundi Rin Samanvay Samiti, Jaora, Distt. Ratlam submits a written complaint signed by various depositors inter-alia alleging that Bherulal Patidar(applicant) has promised to pay interest on their deposits.
Bherulal had executed receipts regarding deposit of money by various complainants.
Mahendra Chandaliya has also recieved deposit of money for Bherulal Patidar and issued receipts.
But, Bherulal and Mahendra Chandaliya did not pay the interest and declined to return the deposited amount.

Thus, Bherulal Patidar and Mahendra Chandaliya have defrauded and misappropriated amount to the tune of Rs.
2,32,50,000/- of various depositors.
On such allegation, the P.S. Jaora registered FIR for offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC and Sections 21(1), 21(2) and 21(3) of the Act of 2019.
The statements of depositors were recorded.
They stated that Mahendra Chandaliya induced them to advance loan to Bherulal Patidar, owner of Firm M/s Ambika Borewell, on promise of payment of interest amount.
Accordingly, they paid cash amount to Bherulal Patidar and Mahendra Chandaliya.
The receipts (promisory notes) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35417 4 MCRC-52117-2025 were given to them.
Initially, they were paid some interest on the amount, but later Bherulal Patidar declined to pay the interest amount to them.
The receipts with regard to deposit of amount mostly issued by the Broker, Mahendra Chandaliya were seized.
Mahendra Chandaliya was arrested on 11.04.2025.
He was extended benefit of regular bail vide order dated 04.07.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 17892/2025.
The investigation is underway.
Applicant is apprehending his arrest in the matter.
The statements of complainant on record prima facie show that they have extended the money as loan to Bherulal Patidar for need in business of his Firm M/S Ambika Borewell.

sentences.text: As informed, the applicant is aged around 73 years.
He is an agriculturist and businessman by profession and has family responsibilities.
Considering the advanced age, profession and status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of fleeing from justice or involving in any criminal activity.

In absence of any criminal antecedents, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with the evidence, influencing the witness or interfering in the investigation by the applicant.
The incarceration of applicant does not appear to be necessary for the purpose of investigation.
The grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant will not cause prejudice to free, fair and full investigation.

Considering his clean past, age, status and profession, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35417 5 MCRC-52117-2025 applicant may suffer hardship and prejudice due to incarceration entailing social disrepute and humiliation.
Considering the overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the accusation, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant - Bherulal Patidar shall be released on bail in connection with Crime as mentioned in first paragraph of this order, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) with separate solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the officer making arrest/the Competent Court for compliance with the following conditions: (For the convenience of understanding by accused and surety, the conditions of bail are reproduced in Hindi as under):-
1) Applicant shall be available for investigation on direction of the Investigation Officer.
